saints.name: Pope St. Julius I
saints.title: Pope
saints.shortBlurb: The pope who sheltered St. Athanasius and stood for Nicaea against the Arian tide…
biography: A Roman by birth, Julius was chosen bishop of Rome on 6 February 337, after the see had stood vacant four months. His pontificate fell in the thick of the Arian controversy: when Athanasius of Alexandria, deposed and driven out by the Arian party, fled to Rome about 340, Julius received him and made his cause his own.

A synod he assembled at Rome about 341, of more than fifty bishops, acquitted Athanasius; and in his letter to the Eastern bishops Julius rebuked them for deposing a bishop without reference to Rome — 'Can you be ignorant,' he wrote, 'that this is the custom, that we should be written to first, so that from here what is just may be defined?'

Through his influence the Council of Sardica was assembled in 343, which vindicated the exiled bishops and confirmed the right of appeal to the Roman see. He built several churches in Rome and died on 12 April 352. A later tradition, resting on a letter now judged spurious, credits him with fixing 25 December as the feast of the Nativity.
saints.knownFor: Defending St. Athanasius and the Nicene faith against Arianism.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain), 12 April
